messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Bulgarian, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Bulgarian line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Ах колко трудно е да се каже какво беше това диво и грубо и плътно дърво което в мисълта възобновява страха!

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (ENG) | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|------------------------|--------| | Ahi | Exclamatory interjection of emotion | Ах | “Ah!” | OK | | quanto | Degree intensifier (“how”) | колко | “how” | OK | | a | Infinitive marker (introduces *dir*) | да | “to (inf.)” | OK | | dir | Verb “to tell / say” | каже | “says / tells” | OK | | qual | Interrogative “what” (content of *dir*) | какво | “what” | OK | | era | Past copula “was” | беше | “was” | OK | | è | Present copula “is” | е | “is” | OK | | **cosa** | Abstract “thing” (subject of *è dura*) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (Bulgarian expresses the idea with the adjective *трудно* without a noun) | | dura | Adjective “hard / difficult” | трудно | “hard / difficult” | OK | | esta | Demonstrative “this” (determiner for *selva*) | това | “this” | OK | | selva | “forest / wood” (the setting) | дърво | “tree / wood” | OK | | selvaggia | “wild” | диво | “wild” | OK | | e (1) | Coordinating conjunction “and” | и | “and” | OK | | aspra | “rough” | грубо | “rough” | OK | | e (2) | Coordinating conjunction “and” | и | “and” | OK | | forte | “strong / dense” | плътно | “dense / thick” | OK | | che | Relative pronoun “which” (refers to *selva*) | което | “which” | OK | | nel | Prepositional phrase “in the” (locates mental domain) | в | “in” | OK | | pensier | Noun “thought” (mental realm) | мисълта | “the thought” | OK | | rinova | Verb “renews / revives” | възобновява | “renews” | OK | | **la** | Definite article for *paura* | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (Bulgarian marks definiteness with the suffix *‑та* on *страха*) | | paura! | Noun “fear” (object of renewal) | страха! | “the fear!” | OK |
### Summary of Issues - **UNNECESSARY**: *cosa*, *la* – Bulgarian does not require a separate noun for “thing” nor a standalone definite article; the meaning is conveyed by the adjective *трудно* and the suffix *‑та* on *страха*. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** problems were detected.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Bulgarian script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Bulgarian text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
